A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SimpleFold. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SimpleFold folding, ensemble-generation, scaling, and ablation results in Tables 1-3, Figure 4, and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds designed/orphan-protein evaluations and self-distillation results in Tables 9-10.

M1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds an experimental self-distillation training variant: a PDB-only SimpleFold-700M generates filtered training targets for two successive models, R1 and R2. The main architecture, losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds evaluations on computationally designed proteins and orphan proteins without known sequence homologs, substantially broadening the tested populations. Existing folding and ensemble datasets remain; self-distillation reuses existing sequence coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The added protein benchmarks use existing comparators AlphaFold2 and ESMFold; Table 10 introduces SimpleFold training ablations. Newly cited ADiT is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols specify 77 orphan targets and 62 designed targets selected using a May 1, 2020 cutoff. The self-distillation comparison holds model size and sequence pool fixed while varying structural training targets and distillation rounds. Previously reported evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's training-data scaling study, v3 adds a direct investigation of dependence on external structural teachers: PDB-only training followed by two self-distillation rounds, evaluated on CAMEO22 and CASP14. Existing loss, sampling, scaling, and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Reporting continues to use aggregate metrics, including means and medians across targets. No seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added; the new description of better LDDT as significant is not accompanied by a test.

E6.justification: Tables 9-10 add substantial benchmark and training-variant results. Designed-protein mean TM-score is 0.852 for SimpleFold-3B, versus 0.831 for AlphaFold2 and 0.839 for ESMFold. Self-distillation R2 obtains mean TM-scores of 0.805/0.649 on CAMEO22/CASP14, compared with 0.829/0.680 using external distilled structures. All retained table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation, losses, sampling equations, and appendix mathematical definitions are unchanged. The added sections introduce empirical experiments and explanatory arguments, not new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about architectural simplicity, scaling, folding, ensemble generation, and efficiency remain. The introduction's contribution bullet now mentions ensemble generation instead of repeating folding performance, but that claim already appeared in v1's abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2 newly argues that external structural teachers help but are not necessary, suggesting MSA as a possible explanation for their remaining advantage. E.1 interprets the new benchmarks as generalization evidence. C.1 attributes ensemble advantages to generative training from scratch without experimentally isolating that cause.

D1.justification: The new self-distillation description specifies pLDDT thresholds above 80 for pretraining and above 85 for finetuning, plus separate confidence modules trained only on PDB. Existing implementation details, hardware information, and code-access statements are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds ADiT, Chowdhury et al.'s benchmark source, and three PDB-related references. New Appendix C.1 expands the existing comparison with AlphaFlow/ESMFlow, emphasizing training from scratch versus finetuning deterministic models, without fundamentally changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: new appendix subsections, accompanying renumbering, limited introduction and related-work edits, and an updated date. The main narrative remains intact. The new C.1 opening accidentally repeats a clause.

P2.justification: Two tables are added; former Tables 9-13 become Tables 11-15. Existing figures are retained with some relocation, and Appendix F headings become separated from their figures. New Table 9 incorrectly labels both dataset blocks 'De Novo', despite describing designed and orphan proteins.

improvement.justification: The designed/orphan evaluations and self-distillation controls strengthen the generalization and training-data arguments beyond v1's existing PDB-only scaling analysis. These provide a useful extension to an already extensive empirical case. The gain is tempered by Table 9's duplicated dataset label and added causal interpretations that the experiments do not isolate.
